sanskrit: tataḥ samantāt paśyāmi śarajālena veṣṭitam amānuṣāṇi cāstrāṇi prayuñjānaṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: Then I saw Dhanañjaya on all sides enveloped in a net of arrows, wielding weapons beyond human power.

sanskrit: samāvṛtā diśo dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavena śitaiḥ śaraiḥ dhanaṃjayasakhātmānaṃ darśayām āsa vai tadā
english: Seeing the directions filled by the son of Pāṇḍu with sharp arrows, he then revealed himself as one whose very self is a friend of Dhanañjaya.

sanskrit: citrasenaḥ pāṇḍavena samāśliṣya paraṃtapaḥ kuśalaṃ paripapraccha taiḥ pṛṣṭaś cāpy anāmayam
english: Citrasena, the scorcher of foes, embraced the son of Pāṇḍu and asked after his welfare; and being asked by them in return, he told of his own well-being.

sanskrit: te sametya tathānyonyaṃ saṃnāhān vipramucya ca ekībhūtās tato vīrā gandharvāḥ saha pāṇḍavaiḥ apūjayetām anyonyaṃ citrasenadhanaṃjayau
english: Having thus met one another and loosened their armour, the Gandharva heroes and the Pāṇḍavas became united; and Citrasena and Dhanañjaya honoured each other mutually.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca citrasenaṃ samāgamya prahasann arjunas tadā idaṃ vacanam aklībam abravīt paravīrahā
english: Duryodhana said: Having met with Citrasena, Arjuna, the slayer of enemy heroes, then spoke these bold words with a smile.

sanskrit: bhrātṝn arhasi no vīra moktuṃ gandharvasattama anarhā dharṣaṇaṃ hīme jīvamāneṣu pāṇḍuṣu
english: "O hero, O best of Gandharvas, you should release our kinsmen. These men do not deserve to be humiliated while the sons of Pāṇḍu yet live."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu gandharvaḥ pāṇḍavena mahātmanā uvāca yat karṇa vayaṃ mantrayanto vinirgatāḥ draṣṭāraḥ sma sukhād dhīnān sadārān pāṇḍavān iti
english: Thus addressed by the high-souled son of Pāṇḍu, the Gandharva replied: "O Karṇa, we had gone out deliberating, intending to see the Pāṇḍavas fallen from prosperity together with their wives."

sanskrit: tasminn uccāryamāṇe tu gandharveṇa vacasy atha bhūmer vivaram anvaicchaṃ praveṣṭuṃ vrīḍayānvitaḥ
english: And when that speech was being uttered by the Gandharva, I then, overcome with shame, sought a cleft in the earth to enter into.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiram athāgamya gandharvāḥ saha pāṇḍavaiḥ asmaddurmantritaṃ tasmai baddhāṃś cāsmān nyavedayan
english: Then the Gandharvas, along with the Pāṇḍavas, came to Yudhiṣṭhira and reported to him our ill-conceived plan and us as prisoners.

sanskrit: strīsamakṣam ahaṃ dīno baddhaḥ śatruvaśaṃ gataḥ yudhiṣṭhirasyopahṛtaḥ kiṃ nu duḥkham ataḥ param
english: Wretched, bound, fallen into the power of enemies, I was brought before Yudhiṣṭhira in the presence of women — what greater sorrow than this could there be?

sanskrit: ye me nirākṛtā nityaṃ ripur yeṣām ahaṃ sadā tair mokṣito 'haṃ durbuddhir dattaṃ tair jīvitaṃ ca me
english: Those whom I always rejected, those whose enemy I ever was — by them I, foolish-minded one, have been released; my very life has been given by them.

sanskrit: prāptaḥ syāṃ yady ahaṃ vīra vadhaṃ tasmin mahāraṇe śreyas tad bhavitā mahyam evaṃbhūtaṃ na jīvitam
english: O hero, if I had met death in that great battle, that would have been better for me — a life such as this is no life at all.

sanskrit: bhaved yaśaḥ pṛthivyāṃ me khyātaṃ gandharvato vadhāt prāptāś ca lokāḥ puṇyāḥ syur mahendrasadane 'kṣayāḥ
english: I would have gained fame on earth celebrated by death at the hands of the Gandharvas, and would have attained meritorious worlds imperishable in the abode of great Indra.

sanskrit: yat tv adya me vyavasitaṃ tac chṛṇudhvaṃ nararṣabhāḥ iha prāyam upāsiṣye yūyaṃ vrajata vai gṛhān bhrātaraś caiva me sarve prayāntv adya puraṃ prati
english: But hear now what I have resolved upon, O best of men: I shall remain here engaged in the fast unto death. You all go home; let all my brothers depart this day toward the city.

sanskrit: karṇaprabhṛtayaś caiva suhṛdo bāndhavāś ca ye duḥśāsanaṃ puraskṛtya prayāntv adya puraṃ prati
english: And Karṇa and the rest, friends and kinsmen — let them all set forth today toward the city, with Duḥśāsana at their head.

sanskrit: na hy ahaṃ pratiyāsyāmi puraṃ śatrunirākṛtaḥ śatrumānāpaho bhūtvā suhṛdāṃ mānakṛt tathā
english: For I shall not return to the city — one who has been humiliated by enemies, who has become a destroyer of his friends' honour and yet himself brought honour to his enemies.

sanskrit: sa suhṛcchokado bhūtvā śatrūṇāṃ harṣavardhanaḥ vāraṇāhvayam āsādya kiṃ vakṣyāmi janādhipam
english: Having caused grief to my friends and increased the joy of my enemies, what shall I say to the lord of men when I reach Hāstinapura?

sanskrit: bhīṣmo droṇaḥ kṛpo drauṇir viduraḥ saṃjayas tathā bāhlīkaḥ somadattaś ca ye cānye vṛddhasaṃmatāḥ
english: Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, Drauṇi, Vidura, Sañjaya, Bāhlīka, Somadatta, and all the other elders held in esteem —

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāḥ śreṇimukhyāś ca tathodāsīnavṛttayaḥ kiṃ māṃ vakṣyanti kiṃ cāpi prativakṣyāmi tān aham
english: Brāhmaṇas, guild leaders, and those who remain neutral — what will they say to me, and what in turn shall I say to them?

sanskrit: ripūṇāṃ śirasi sthitvā tathā vikramya corasi ātmadoṣāt paribhraṣṭaḥ kathaṃ vakṣyāmi tān aham
english: Having once stood upon the heads of my enemies and having trodden upon their chests, now fallen from that height through my own fault — how shall I speak to them?

sanskrit: durvinītāḥ śriyaṃ prāpya vidyām aiśvaryam eva ca tiṣṭhanti na ciraṃ bhadre yathāhaṃ madagarvitaḥ
english: The arrogant, having obtained prosperity, learning, and lordship, do not endure for long, O auspicious one — even as I, puffed up with pride.

sanskrit: aho bata yathedaṃ me kaṣṭaṃ duścaritaṃ kṛtam svayaṃ durbuddhinā mohād yena prāpto 'smi saṃśayam
english: Alas, what a painful, evil deed I myself have done with foolish understanding and delusion, by which I have reached this peril.

sanskrit: tasmāt prāyam upāsiṣye na hi śakṣyāmi jīvitum cetayāno hi ko jīvet kṛcchrāc chatrubhir uddhṛtaḥ
english: Therefore I shall remain in the fast unto death; for I cannot live. Indeed what conscious man could live, having been rescued from distress by his enemies?

sanskrit: śatrubhiś cāvahasito mānī pauruṣavarjitaḥ pāṇḍavair vikramāḍhyaiś ca sāvamānam avekṣitaḥ
english: Mocked by enemies, bereft of manliness, I who was proud — looked upon with contempt by the mighty Pāṇḍavas of great heroism.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ cintāparigato duḥśāsanam athābravīt duḥśāsana nibodhedaṃ vacanaṃ mama bhārata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus overwhelmed with grief, he then spoke to Duḥśāsana: "Duḥśāsana, hear this my word, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: pratīccha tvaṃ mayā dattam abhiṣekaṃ nṛpo bhava praśādhi pṛthivīṃ sphītāṃ karṇasaubalapālitām
english: Accept the consecration given by me; become king; rule this prosperous earth, protected by Karṇa and Śaubala.

sanskrit: bhrātṝn pālaya visrabdhaṃ maruto vṛtrahā yathā bāndhavās tvopajīvantu devā iva śatakratum
english: Protect your brothers with confidence, as Vṛtrahā protects the Maruts; let kinsmen live under you as the gods under Śatakratu.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇeṣu sadā vṛttiṃ kurvīthāś cāpramādataḥ bandhūnāṃ suhṛdāṃ caiva bhavethās tvaṃ gatiḥ sadā
english: Always provide support for the Brāhmaṇas diligently; be ever the refuge of kinsmen and friends.

sanskrit: jñātīṃś cāpy anupaśyethā viṣṇur devagaṇān iva guravaḥ pālanīyās te gaccha pālaya medinīm
english: Watch over your relatives as Viṣṇu watches over the hosts of gods; the elders are to be protected by you — go, protect the earth.

sanskrit: nandayan suhṛdaḥ sarvāñ śātravāṃś cāvabhartsayan kaṇṭhe cainaṃ pariṣvajya gamyatām ity uvāca ha
english: Gladdening all friends and rebuking foes" — embracing him about the neck, he said, "Go."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā dīno duḥśāsano 'bravīt aśrukaṇṭhaḥ suduḥkhārtaḥ prāñjaliḥ praṇipatya ca sagadgadam idaṃ vākyaṃ bhrātaraṃ jyeṣṭham ātmanaḥ
english: Hearing those words, wretched Duḥśāsana spoke — his throat choked with tears, sorely afflicted with grief, having bowed down with joined palms — these stammering words to his eldest brother:

sanskrit: prasīdety apatad bhūmau dūyamānena cetasā duḥkhitaḥ pādayos tasya netrajaṃ jalam utsṛjan
english: "Be gracious" — and he fell to the ground with anguished heart, grief-stricken, pouring tears from his eyes at his feet.

sanskrit: uktavāṃś ca naravyāghro naitad evaṃ bhaviṣyati vidīryet sanagā bhūmir dyauś cāpi śakalībhavet ravir ātmaprabhāṃ jahyāt somaḥ śītāṃśutāṃ tyajet
english: And the tiger among men declared: "This shall never be so. The earth with all its trees may split asunder; the sky may shatter into fragments; the sun may abandon its own radiance; the moon may forsake its coolness —

sanskrit: vāyuḥ śaighryam atho jahyād dhimavāṃś ca parivrajet śuṣyet toyaṃ samudreṣu vahnir apy uṣṇatāṃ tyajet
english: The wind may abandon its swiftness and the Himālaya may wander; the waters of the oceans may dry up and fire may forsake its heat —

sanskrit: na cāhaṃ tvad ṛte rājan praśāseyaṃ vasuṃdharām punaḥ punaḥ prasīdeti vākyaṃ cedam uvāca ha tvam eva naḥ kule rājā bhaviṣyasi śataṃ samāḥ
english: Yet I shall not rule the earth without you, O king" — and repeatedly speaking these words "Be gracious," he said: "You alone shall be king in our family for a hundred years."

sanskrit: evam uktvā sa rājendra sasvanaṃ praruroda ha pādau saṃgṛhya mānārhau bhrātur jyeṣṭhasya bhārata
english: Having spoken thus, O lord of kings, he burst into loud weeping, O Bhārata, clasping the worthy feet of his eldest brother.

sanskrit: tathā tau duḥkhitau dṛṣṭvā duḥśāsanasuyodhanau abhigamya vyathāviṣṭaḥ karṇas tau pratyabhāṣata
english: Seeing those two in such distress — Duḥśāsana and Suyodhana — Karṇa, filled with anguish, approached and addressed them both.

sanskrit: viṣīdathaḥ kiṃ kauravyau bāliśyāt prākṛtāv iva na śokaḥ śocamānasya vinivarteta kasya cit
english: "Why do you two Kaurava princes grieve like common men, lacking wisdom? Grief never departs from one who grieves — of whom has it ever turned back?

sanskrit: yadā ca śocataḥ śoko vyasanaṃ nāpakarṣati sāmarthyaṃ kiṃ tv ataḥ śoke śocamānau prapaśyathaḥ dhṛtiṃ gṛhṇīta mā śatrūñ śocantau nandayiṣyathaḥ
english: And when grief does not remove the calamity of one who grieves, what efficacy then do you two see in grieving? Take hold of fortitude — do not gladden your enemies by grieving."

sanskrit: kartavyaṃ hi kṛtaṃ rājan pāṇḍavais tava mokṣaṇam nityam eva priyaṃ kāryaṃ rājño viṣayavāsibhiḥ pālyamānās tvayā te hi nivasanti gatajvarāḥ
english: "O king, the Pāṇḍavas have done what was their duty in freeing you. Those who dwell in a king's realm must always perform what is agreeable to the king; protected by you, they dwell without anxiety.

sanskrit: nārhasy evaṃgate manyuṃ kartuṃ prākṛtavad yathā viṣaṇṇās tava sodaryās tvayi prāyaṃ samāsthite uttiṣṭha vraja bhadraṃ te samāśvāsaya sodarān
english: You ought not, in these circumstances, to give way to anger like a common man. Your brothers are distressed while you are set on the fast unto death — rise, go, may it be well with you, comfort your brothers.

sanskrit: rājann adyāvagacchāmi taveha laghusattvatām kim atra citraṃ yad vīra mokṣitaḥ pāṇḍavair asi sadyo vaśaṃ samāpannaḥ śatrūṇāṃ śatrukarśana
english: O king, I now perceive your faint-heartedness here. What is remarkable in this, O hero, that you were freed by the Pāṇḍavas? You quickly fell into the power of enemies, O chastiser of foes.

sanskrit: senājīvaiś ca kauravya tathā viṣayavāsibhiḥ ajñātair yadi vā jñātaiḥ kartavyaṃ nṛpateḥ priyam
english: O Kaurava, by those who live by soldiery and those who dwell in the realm — whether known or unknown — what is pleasing to the king must be done.

sanskrit: prāyaḥ pradhānāḥ puruṣāḥ kṣobhayanty arivāhinīm nigṛhyante ca yuddheṣu mokṣyante ca svasainikaiḥ
english: Generally chief men do stir up the enemy's army; they are also captured in battles and freed by their own soldiers.

sanskrit: senājīvāś ca ye rājñāṃ viṣaye santi mānavāḥ taiḥ saṃgamya nṛpārthāya yatitavyaṃ yathātatham
english: And those men who live as soldiers within a king's realm — uniting with them, one must strive duly for the king's benefit.

sanskrit: yady evaṃ pāṇḍavai rājan bhavadviṣayavāsibhiḥ yadṛcchayā mokṣito 'dya tatra kā paridevanā
english: If you were thus freed today by the Pāṇḍavas and by those dwelling in your realm by chance, what lamentation is there in that?

sanskrit: na caitat sādhu yad rājan pāṇḍavās tvāṃ nṛpottama svasenayā saṃprayāntaṃ nānuyānti sma pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: And it was not good, O king, O best of rulers, that the Pāṇḍavas did not follow behind you when you were departing with your own army.

sanskrit: śūrāś ca balavantaś ca saṃyugeṣv apalāyinaḥ bhavatas te sabhāyāṃ vai preṣyatāṃ pūrvam āgatāḥ
english: Those heroes who are brave, powerful, and do not flee in battle — those servants of yours came to the assembly hall formerly.

sanskrit: pāṇḍaveyāni ratnāni tvam adyāpy upabhuñjase sattvasthān pāṇḍavān paśya na te prāyam upāviśan uttiṣṭha rājan bhadraṃ te na cintāṃ kartum arhasi
english: You even now enjoy the jewels that came from the Pāṇḍavas. See the Pāṇḍavas — they are steadfast; they did not sit in fasting. Rise, O king, may it be well with you — you ought not to grieve.

sanskrit: avaśyam eva nṛpate rājño viṣayavāsibhiḥ priyāṇy ācaritavyāni tatra kā paridevanā
english: O lord of kings, those who dwell in a king's realm must certainly do what is pleasing to him — what lamentation is there in that?

sanskrit: madvākyam etad rājendra yady evaṃ na kariṣyasi sthāsyāmīha bhavatpādau śuśrūṣann arimardana
english: This is my word, O lord of kings — if you do not act thus, I shall remain here serving your feet, O crusher of enemies.

sanskrit: notsahe jīvitum ahaṃ tvadvihīno nararṣabha prāyopaviṣṭas tu nṛpa rājñāṃ hāsyo bhaviṣyasi
english: O best of men, I have no wish to live without you. But O king, one who sits in fasting unto death becomes an object of ridicule among kings.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tu karṇena rājā duryodhanas tadā naivotthātuṃ manaś cakre svargāya kṛtaniścayaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by Karṇa, king Duryodhana at that time had no mind to rise — he was firmly resolved upon heaven.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca prāyopaviṣṭaṃ rājānaṃ duryodhanam amarṣaṇam uvāca sāntvayan rājañ śakuniḥ saubalas tadā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Śakuni, the son of Subala, spoke consoling words to king Duryodhana, the impatient one, who was seated in the fast unto death.

sanskrit: samyag uktaṃ hi karṇena tac chrutaṃ kaurava tvayā mayāhṛtāṃ śriyaṃ sphītāṃ mohāt samapahāya kim tvam abuddhyā nṛpavara prāṇān utsraṣṭum icchasi
english: "What Karṇa has said is right and you have heard it, O Kaurava. Having cast away through delusion the great prosperity I brought you, why do you, O best of kings, foolishly wish to abandon your life?

sanskrit: adya cāpy avagacchāmi na vṛddhāḥ sevitās tvayā yaḥ samutpatitaṃ harṣaṃ dainyaṃ vā na niyacchati sa naśyati śriyaṃ prāpya pātram āmam ivāmbhasi
english: And I understand now that you have not attended upon the elders. He who does not restrain sudden elation or dejection perishes after gaining prosperity, like a raw vessel in water.

sanskrit: atibhīrum atiklībaṃ dīrghasūtraṃ pramādinam vyasanād viṣayākrāntaṃ na bhajanti nṛpaṃ śriyaḥ
english: The overly fearful, the utterly feeble, the procrastinator, the negligent, and one overwhelmed by addiction and sensual pleasures — prosperity does not attend such a king.

sanskrit: satkṛtasya hi te śoko viparīte kathaṃ bhavet mā kṛtaṃ śobhanaṃ pārthaiḥ śokam ālambya nāśaya
english: For you who have been honoured, how can there be grief in a reversal? Do not, by clinging to grief, destroy the good that has been done by the Pārthas.

sanskrit: yatra harṣas tvayā kāryaḥ satkartavyāś ca pāṇḍavāḥ tatra śocasi rājendra viparītam idaṃ tava
english: Where you should feel joy and the Pāṇḍavas should be honoured, there you grieve, O lord of kings — this is contrary for you.

sanskrit: prasīda mā tyajātmānaṃ tuṣṭaś ca sukṛtaṃ smara prayaccha rājyaṃ pārthānāṃ yaśo dharmam avāpnuhi
english: Be gracious; do not abandon yourself; in a spirit of contentment, remember the good done; bestow the kingdom upon the Pārthas and win fame and righteousness.

sanskrit: kriyām etāṃ samājñāya kṛtaghno na bhaviṣyasi saubhrātraṃ pāṇḍavaiḥ kṛtvā samavasthāpya caiva tān pitryaṃ rājyaṃ prayacchaiṣāṃ tataḥ sukham avāpnuhi
english: Knowing this act rightly, you will not become ungrateful. Having established brotherhood with the Pāṇḍavas and settling them, bestow on them their paternal kingdom — then attain happiness.

sanskrit: śakunes tu vacaḥ śrutvā duḥśāsanam avekṣya ca pādayoḥ patitaṃ vīraṃ viklavaṃ bhrātṛsauhṛdāt
english: Hearing the words of Śakuni and looking at Duḥśāsana — the hero fallen at his feet, distressed out of fraternal affection —

sanskrit: bāhubhyāṃ sādhujātābhyāṃ duḥśāsanam ariṃdamam utthāpya saṃpariṣvajya prītyājighrata mūrdhani
english: He raised up Duḥśāsana, the crusher of foes, with his well-formed arms, embraced him, and with affection smelt his head.

sanskrit: karṇasaubalayoś cāpi saṃsmṛtya vacanāny asau nirvedaṃ paramaṃ gatvā rājā duryodhanas tadā vrīḍayābhiparītātmā nairāśyam agamat param
english: And reflecting on the words of Karṇa and Śaubala as well, king Duryodhana at that time, his soul overwhelmed with shame, reached a state of utter disgust and supreme despondency.

sanskrit: suhṛdāṃ caiva tac chrutvā samanyur idam abravīt na dharmadhanasaukhyena naiśvaryeṇa na cājñayā naiva bhogaiś ca me kāryaṃ mā vihanyata gacchata
english: And having heard that from his friends, he spoke this with anger: "I have no need of righteousness, wealth, happiness, lordship, command, or enjoyments — do not be hindered, go."

sanskrit: niściteyaṃ mama matiḥ sthitā prāyopaveśane gacchadhvaṃ nagaraṃ sarve pūjyāś ca guravo mama
english: "This is my firm resolve, fixed in the fast unto death. All of you go to the city — my elders too are to be honoured."

sanskrit: ta evam uktāḥ pratyūcū rājānam arimardanam yā gatis tava rājendra sāsmākam api bhārata kathaṃ vā saṃpravekṣyāmas tvadvihīnāḥ puraṃ vayam
english: Those thus addressed replied to the king, the crusher of enemies: "Whatever course you take, O lord of kings, that is ours as well, O Bhārata. How would we enter the city bereft of you?"

sanskrit: sa suhṛdbhir amātyaiś ca bhrātṛbhiḥ svajanena ca bahuprakāram apy ukto niścayān na vyacālyata
english: Though thus addressed in many ways by friends, ministers, brothers, and kinsmen, he did not waver from his resolve.

sanskrit: darbhaprastaram āstīrya niścayād dhṛtarāṣṭrajaḥ saṃspṛśyāpaḥ śucir bhūtvā bhūtalaṃ samupāśritaḥ
english: Spreading out a bed of kuśa grass by firm resolve, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, having touched water and become pure, sat down upon the ground.

sanskrit: kuśacīrāmbaradharaḥ paraṃ niyamam āsthitaḥ vāgyato rājaśārdūlaḥ sa svargagatikāṅkṣayā manasopacitiṃ kṛtvā nirasya ca bahiṣkriyāḥ
english: Wearing kuśa grass and bark garments, the tiger among kings undertook supreme discipline — controlling his speech, concentrating his mind, and discarding all external actions, aspiring for the path to heaven.

sanskrit: atha taṃ niścayaṃ tasya buddhvā daiteyadānavāḥ pātālavāsino raudrāḥ pūrvaṃ devair vinirjitāḥ
english: Then, having learned of that resolve of his, the fearsome Daityas and Dānavas dwelling in the nether world, formerly defeated by the gods —

sanskrit: te svapakṣakṣayaṃ taṃ tu jñātvā duryodhanasya vai āhvānāya tadā cakruḥ karma vaitānasaṃbhavam
english: They, knowing that destruction of their own faction through Duryodhana's fate, then performed a sacrificial rite in order to summon him.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatyuśanoktaiś ca mantrair mantraviśāradāḥ atharvavedaproktaiś ca yāś copaniṣadi kriyāḥ mantrajapyasamāyuktās tās tadā samavartayan
english: Expert in sacred formulas, they then performed those rites, combined with repetition of mantras — with the chants prescribed by Bṛhaspati and Uśanas, and those enjoined in the Atharvaveda and the Upaniṣads.

sanskrit: juhvaty agnau haviḥ kṣīraṃ mantravat susamāhitāḥ brāhmaṇā vedavedāṅgapāragāḥ sudṛḍhavratāḥ
english: Brāhmaṇas who had mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, firm in their vows, well concentrated, poured oblations and milk into the fire in accordance with sacred formulas.

sanskrit: karmasiddhau tadā tatra jṛmbhamāṇā mahādbhutā kṛtyā samutthitā rājan kiṃ karomīti cābravīt
english: When the rite was accomplished, there then arose, yawning, a great and wondrous female demon-power; and she said, O king, "What shall I do?"

sanskrit: āhur daityāś ca tāṃ tatra suprītenāntarātmanā prāyopaviṣṭaṃ rājānaṃ dhārtarāṣṭram ihānaya
english: And the Daityas there said to her with inwardly delighted hearts: "Bring here the king, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, who is seated in the fast unto death."

sanskrit: tatheti ca pratiśrutya sā kṛtyā prayayau tadā nimeṣād agamac cāpi yatra rājā suyodhanaḥ
english: Assenting with "So be it," that female demon-power then departed; and in the twinkling of an eye she reached where king Suyodhana was.

sanskrit: samādāya ca rājānaṃ praviveśa rasātalam dānavānāṃ muhūrtāc ca tam ānītaṃ nyavedayat
english: Taking up the king, she entered the nether world, and within a moment she reported to the Dānavas that he had been brought.

sanskrit: tam ānītaṃ nṛpaṃ dṛṣṭvā rātrau saṃhatya dānavāḥ prahṛṣṭamanasaḥ sarve kiṃ cid utphullalocanāḥ sābhimānam idaṃ vākyaṃ duryodhanam athābruvan
english: Seeing the king thus brought, the Dānavas assembled at night, all with joyful hearts and somewhat wide-opened eyes, and then spoke these proud words to Duryodhana:

sanskrit: dānavā ūcuḥ bhoḥ suyodhana rājendra bharatānāṃ kulodvaha śūraiḥ parivṛto nityaṃ tathaiva ca mahātmabhiḥ
english: The Dānavas said: O Suyodhana, O lord of kings, O upholder of the Bharata lineage, you are ever surrounded by heroes and high-souled men alike.
